scenario: 调度系统里「发邮件」要被上千用户按各自时间复用，因此必须把「做什么」单独建模。
scenario_en: In the scheduler, send-email has to be reused by thousands of users at their own times, so what-to-do must be modeled on its own.
q: 在任务调度系统里，「Task（任务）」的准确定义是？
q_en: In a job scheduler, what's the precise definition of a Task?
options: 一次绑定了具体执行时间和参数的执行实例
抽象的、可复用的「要做的工作」，可被多个 Job 反复执行
用来触发周期性执行的 CRON 表达式规则，只表达时间规律，不代表任务本身要做什么
记录某次执行状态和结果的数据库行
why: Task 是抽象、可复用的工作定义（如「发邮件」），本身不含时间和收件人；它可以被不同 Job 反复调用。
why_en: A task is the abstract, reusable unit of work like send-email, which can be executed many times by different jobs.
options_en: A single execution instance bound to a concrete time and parameters.
The abstract, reusable unit of work that many jobs can execute.
A CRON expression rule used to trigger periodic execution., saying only when things repeat, not what the task itself does.
A database row that records one execution's status and result.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用固定语法表示周期性时间规则的表达式，如「每天 10 点」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CRON expression is a fixed syntax for describing a recurring schedule, like every day at ten.

optionExplanations: 这其实是 Job 的样子：一旦 Task 绑上具体执行时间和参数，才变成一次可调度的 Job。
对，Task 是可复用的抽象工作定义，本身不带时间和收件人，靠 Job 赋予具体调度。
这是 Schedule 承载的内容：CRON 表达的是「何时」，不是任务本身是什么。
这是一条执行记录：保存的是某次运行的状态和结果，不是任务的定义。
optionExplanations_en: That's actually what a job looks like — a task only becomes schedulable once it's bound to a time and parameters.
Right: a task is the reusable, abstract unit of work, with no time or recipient baked in until a job adds them.
That's what Schedule carries — CRON expresses when, not what the task itself is.
That's an execution record, storing one run's status and result, not the task definition.

scenario: 同一个「发邮件」定义要衍生出「周五 10:00 发给 john」这样成千上万次具体调度。
scenario_en: The same send-email definition has to spawn thousands of concrete runs like Friday 10:00 to john.
q: 在「抽象 vs 实例」这个维度上，Job 和 Task 的区别是？
q_en: On the abstract-versus-instance axis, what's the difference between a Job and a Task?
options: Job 才是抽象的工作定义，Task 只是它的一次具体执行，且完全不需要绑定任何调度时间或参数
Job 是 Task 的一个实例：绑定了具体的 Task、调度时间和参数
两者在系统语义里完全等价，只是换了一种叫法而已
Task 本身携带执行时间和参数，而 Job 完全不携带
why: Job 是 Task 的实例，把「发邮件」这个 Task 加上「周五 10:00 发给 john」这样的时间与参数，才构成一个可调度的 Job。
why_en: A job is an instance of a task, pairing the task with a schedule and the parameters needed to run it.
tradeoff: Task（抽象定义） vs Job（绑定时间与参数的实例）
options_en: A job is actually the abstract work definition, and a task is just one concrete execution of it., with no schedule or parameters attached to it at all.
A job is an instance of a task, bound to a schedule and parameters.
The two terms are fully equivalent in the system's semantics, just a different name.
A task itself carries the execution time and parameters, while a job carries none at all.
optionExplanations: 说反了，抽象定义是 Task，Job 才是绑定了时间和参数的那次具体执行。
对，Job 把 Task 加上调度时间和参数，才变成一个可执行的实例。
两者职责不同：一个是可复用定义，一个是绑定参数的执行实例，并不等价。
又说反了，时间和参数是挂在 Job 上的，Task 本身并不携带它们。
optionExplanations_en: That's backwards — the abstract definition is the task, and a job is the concrete run of it.
Right: a job takes a task and attaches a schedule and parameters, turning it into something runnable.
They play different roles — one's a reusable definition, the other's a bound instance — not the same thing.
Backwards again — schedule and parameters live on the job, not on the task itself.

q: 补全任务调度系统的两条核心功能需求：
q_en: Fill in the two core functional requirements for this job scheduler:
text: 用户可以调度 Job 在{{立即}}、{{未来某个时间}}或按{{周期性}}计划执行；用户可以{{监控}}自己 Job 的状态。
why: 两条功能需求：灵活调度（立即 / 未来 / 周期性）+ 状态监控。取消或重排 Job 属于范围外（below the line）。
why_en: The two core functional requirements are scheduling jobs immediately, at a future time, or recurring, and monitoring job status.

scenario: 面试官说系统要保证在调度失败时仍能对外服务，问在可用性和一致性之间怎么取舍。
scenario_en: The interviewer says the system must keep serving requests even when scheduling fails, and asks how you'd trade off availability against consistency.
q: 这个任务调度系统应优先保证哪一个？
q_en: Which should this job scheduler prioritize?
options: 应当优先保证强一致性，即使牺牲一部分可用性也在所不惜，哪怕因此让调度延迟或短暂停止对外服务
高可用优先（availability > consistency）
可用性和一致性在这个场景里都同样无关紧要
只需要保证足够低的延迟，完全不用考虑系统可用性
why: 调度系统选择高可用优先于一致性：宁可偶尔重复或稍有不一致，也要保证 Job 能被接收和执行。这也是后面选 DynamoDB / Cassandra 的依据。
why_en: The scheduler prioritizes high availability over strong consistency, which justifies choosing an AP-style key-value store.
whenOtherWins: 如果是转账、库存扣减这类必须精确一次且强一致的核心账务系统，一致性才该压过可用性。
tradeoff: 高可用（宁可偶尔重复/不一致） vs 强一致性（保证唯一且最新）
options_en: Strong consistency should come first, even at the cost of some availability., even if that means scheduling stalls or briefly stops serving requests.
Prioritize high availability over consistency.
In this scenario, neither availability nor consistency really matters.
Only guarantee sufficiently low latency, without considering availability at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统始终能响应请求的能力，即使部分节点故障。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Availability is a system's ability to keep responding even when some nodes fail.

termDefinitions.meaning: 所有节点在同一时刻看到相同、最新的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistency means all nodes see the same up-to-date data at the same time.

optionExplanations: 在转账、扣库存这类必须精确一次的强一致场景更该选它，但这里的目标是调度别失联，用不上。
对，调度系统宁可偶尔重复或数据稍旧，也要保证 Job 在失败时依然能被接收和执行。
可用性和一致性都是要花代价买的属性，场景已经明确要保服务不中断，不是可以随便丢的。
题目问的是可用性 vs 一致性这条轴，低延迟是另一回事，不能替换掉这个取舍。
optionExplanations_en: That fits a must-be-exactly-once system like payments or inventory, but here the goal is staying reachable, not that.
Right: the scheduler accepts occasional duplicates or slightly stale reads so jobs keep getting accepted and run even when something fails.
Availability and consistency both cost something to guarantee — the scenario explicitly needs uptime, so neither is free to ignore.
The question is availability versus consistency, not latency — swapping in a different axis doesn't answer it.

scenario: 面试官报出该系统的三条硬性非功能指标，作为后续所有深潜的输入条件。
scenario_en: The interviewer states three hard non-functional targets for the system, which become the inputs for every deep dive that follows.
q: 补全本题的关键非功能指标：
q_en: Fill in the key non-functional requirements:
text: 系统要支持每秒 {{10k}} 个 Job，执行时间误差在调度时间的 {{2}} 秒内，并保证 {{at-least-once}}（至少一次）执行。
why: 三个硬指标锚点：吞吐 10k jobs/s、精度 2 秒内、至少一次执行。它们分别驱动了后面的分片、两层调度、重试三个深潜。
why_en: The system targets ten thousand jobs per second, execution within two seconds of schedule, and at-least-once execution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证消息或任务至少被处理一次，但可能重复处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: At-least-once delivery guarantees a message is processed at least once, but possibly more than once.

scenario: 非功能需求明确：Job 必须在其调度时间的 2 秒内被执行。
scenario_en: A non-functional requirement states jobs must execute within two seconds of their scheduled time.
q: 这条 2 秒精度指标，从设计角度直接排除了哪种朴素做法？
q_en: Which naive approach does this two-second precision requirement directly rule out?
options: 每隔几分钟轮询数据库一次找待执行 Job
用消息队列缓冲要执行的 Job
给 Executions 表按时间建索引
对新建 Job 的写请求做限流
why: 轮询间隔本身就是精度的天花板：几分钟一轮意味着最坏几分钟的偏差，2 秒精度必须换成别的机制。
why_en: A polling interval caps precision, so minute-level polling cannot meet a two-second requirement.
options_en: Poll the database every few minutes for due jobs.
Buffer due jobs in a message queue.
Add a time index on the Executions table.
Rate-limit write requests for new jobs.
optionExplanations: 对，多久检查一次待办 Job 就是误差能有多大的上限，分钟级检查天然够不到 2 秒这条线。
消息队列本身不是精度瓶颈，真正卡精度的是发现『该跑了』这件事的检测频率。
加索引只让查询本身更快，改变不了轮询多久查一次这个根本上限。
限流管的是新建 Job 的写入速率，跟已建好的 Job 何时被执行没关系。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the polling interval is the ceiling on precision — a few minutes between polls means minutes of possible drift, and that blows the 2-second budget.
A queue by itself isn't the precision bottleneck — the real limiter is how often you check for due work in the first place.
An index just makes each query faster; it doesn't change how often you're running that query.
Rate limiting caps how fast new jobs get created — it has nothing to do with when an existing job actually runs.

scenario: 面试官要你在画高层设计前先列实体：用户自建 Job、按 CRON 周期执行、还要能查状态。
scenario_en: Before the high-level design the interviewer wants the entity list: users create jobs, they run on CRON, and status must be queryable.
q: 本系统的核心实体（entities）包括以下哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which of the following are core entities in this system? (select all)
options: Task（任务定义）
Job（任务实例）
Schedule（CRON 或具体时间）
User（调度并查看 Job 的用户）
why: 四个核心实体：Task、Job、Schedule、User。前期只列清单、不纠结列名，等高层设计时再细化字段。
why_en: The core entities are Task, Job, Schedule, and User, listed broadly before detailing columns.
options_en: Task, the reusable work definition.
Job, an instance of a task.
Schedule, a CRON expression or a specific time.
User, who schedules and views jobs.
optionExplanations: 对，Task 是可被反复复用的工作定义，是这套模型里最底层的抽象。
对，Job 把 Task 绑上具体时间和参数，是真正会被调度执行的那个东西。
对，Schedule 承载「何时执行」，用 CRON 或具体 DateTime 表达。
对，User 是发起调度、查看自己 Job 状态的一方，串起权限和查询范围。
optionExplanations_en: Right: Task is the reusable definition of the work — the bottom layer of this model.
Right: Job binds a task to a concrete time and parameters — it's the thing that actually gets scheduled.
Right: Schedule carries when to run, expressed as a CRON expression or a specific DateTime.
Right: User is who creates jobs and checks their status, anchoring query scope and permissions.

scenario: 实体清单里已有 Task（做什么）和 Job（一次调度），还缺一个实体回答「何时执行」。
scenario_en: The entity list already has Task (what to do) and Job (one run); one entity is still missing to answer when it fires.
q: Schedule 实体承载的是什么？
q_en: What does the Schedule entity represent?
options: 任务在被调度前实际要运行的那段业务代码逻辑，这部分内容其实由 Task 承载，跟执行时间无关
Job 何时执行：一个 CRON 表达式或一个具体 DateTime
用户登录调度系统时使用的账号身份凭证信息
记录任务每一次具体执行结果的历史日志条目
why: Schedule 表示「何时执行」，用 CRON 表达式表示周期性，或用具体 DateTime 表示一次性。
why_en: The Schedule entity captures when a job runs, either a CRON expression or a specific datetime.
options_en: The actual business code logic the task runs once scheduled., which actually belongs to Task, not to when something runs.
When a job runs: a CRON expression or a specific datetime.
The account credentials a user logs into the scheduling system with.
A historical log entry recording each concrete execution's result.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用固定语法表示周期性时间规则的表达式，如「每天 10 点」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CRON expression is a fixed syntax for describing a recurring schedule, like every day at ten.

optionExplanations: 这是 Task 承载的内容：真正要跑的业务逻辑，不属于 Schedule。
对，Schedule 回答的是『什么时候该跑』，周期性写成 CRON，单次就用一个具体时间点。
这是身份认证信息，跟「何时执行」这个调度语义完全不搭边。
这是 Execution 记录的内容：某次运行留下的历史结果，不是调度规则本身。
optionExplanations_en: That's what Task carries — the actual business logic to run — not what Schedule is for.
Right: Schedule is when to run, a CRON expression for recurring jobs or a specific DateTime for one-off ones.
That's login credential info — it has nothing to do with when a job runs.
That's what an Execution record holds — the history of one run — not the scheduling rule itself.

scenario: 功能需求是「用户能创建按 CRON 周期执行的 Job」，接口设计要与该需求 1:1 对应。
scenario_en: The functional requirement is that users create jobs on a CRON schedule, and the API should map one-to-one onto it.
q: 创建 Job 的接口大致是怎样的？
q_en: Roughly what does the create-job API look like?
options: GET /jobs 不带任何过滤条件，直接返回系统里全部的 Job 记录，且不支持任何分页或权限校验
POST /jobs，携带 task_id、schedule（CRON）和 parameters
PUT /tasks/{task_id}，用来修改某个任务本身的执行代码
DELETE /jobs/{id}，用来取消一个已经创建好的 Job
why: 创建 Job 用 POST /jobs，body 里带 task_id、schedule（如 CRON "0 10 * * *"）和执行参数。接口通常与功能需求 1:1 对应。
why_en: Creating a job is a POST to slash-jobs carrying the task id, a schedule, and the parameters.
options_en: GET /jobs with no filters at all, returning every job record in the system., with no pagination or permission checks at all.
POST /jobs carrying task_id, a schedule (CRON), and parameters.
PUT /tasks/{task_id}, used to modify a task's own executable code.
DELETE /jobs/{id}, used to cancel a job that has already been created.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用固定语法表示周期性时间规则的表达式，如「每天 10 点」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CRON expression is a fixed syntax for describing a recurring schedule, like every day at ten.

optionExplanations: 这是查列表用的 GET，创建资源该用 POST，方法都用错了。
对，新建 Job 是一次 POST 请求，要在请求体里把任务、时间规则和参数一次交齐，三者缺一不可。
这是在改 Task 本身的执行代码，不是在为它排一次新的调度。
这是取消操作，而且取消本就被划在这版范围之外。
optionExplanations_en: That's a GET for listing everything — creating a resource is a POST, so the verb itself is wrong.
Right: creating a job is a POST to /jobs, with task_id, schedule, and parameters all required in the body.
That edits the task's own code, not scheduling a new run of it.
That's a cancel operation, and cancellation was already scoped out of this version.

scenario: 功能需求「用户监控自己 Job 的状态」，前端要按状态和时间区间筛出几百条记录。
scenario_en: Users need to monitor their own jobs, with the UI filtering hundreds of records by status and time range.
q: 查询某用户 Job 状态的接口，最合理的形态是？
q_en: What's the most sensible shape for the API that queries a user's job statuses?
options: POST /jobs/query，请求体里直接拼一段原始 SQL 交给数据库跑
GET /jobs 按 user_id/status/时间区间过滤
GET /jobs/{job_id}，一次只能查一个，还得前端自己拼循环调用
WebSocket 订阅全部 Job 的实时事件，靠前端自己筛出目标用户
why: 监控用 GET /jobs，按 user_id 过滤，并支持 status、时间范围过滤，返回 Job 列表。它对应「监控状态」这条功能需求。
why_en: Status monitoring is a GET on slash-jobs filtered by user id, status, and a time range, returning a list of jobs.
options_en: POST /jobs/query, with the request body concatenating a raw SQL string straight into the database.
GET /jobs filtered by user_id, status, and a time range.
GET /jobs/{job_id}, one job per call, forcing the frontend to loop over ids itself.
A WebSocket subscription to every job's events, with the frontend filtering out its own user.
optionExplanations: 把原始 SQL 直接拼进请求体交给数据库执行，SQL 注入风险大，也不是 REST 该有的形状。
对，GET /jobs 按 user_id 过滤，配合 status 和时间区间，正好对应监控需求。
一次只能查一个 job_id，前端得自己写循环调用，没法一次性回答「这个用户所有 Job 状态」这种列表问题。
订阅全部 Job 的事件流、再靠前端自己按 user_id 过滤，对『查某用户状态』这种一次性查询来说是杀鸡用牛刀，还浪费带宽。
optionExplanations_en: Concatenating raw SQL straight into the request body and handing it to the database is a SQL-injection risk and not how a REST API should look.
Right: GET /jobs filtered by user_id, plus status and a time range, matches the monitoring requirement directly.
That only fetches one job_id at a time and pushes the looping onto the frontend — it can't answer 'all of this user's job statuses' in one call.
Subscribing to every job's event stream and filtering by user_id on the frontend is overkill and wastes bandwidth for a one-shot query like 'check this user's status'.

q: 把 Job 从创建到完成的基本数据流排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the basic data flow of a job from creation to completion:
steps: Worker 在调度时间取走 Job 并执行（失败则指数退避重试）
用户提交 Job：任务、调度时间、参数
更新 Job 在系统中的状态
把 Job 持久化到系统里
why: 基础数据流：用户提交 → 持久化 → Worker 到点取走执行（失败退避重试）→ 更新状态。先建这条简单主线，再逐步增强。
why_en: The basic data flow is submit, persist, execute at scheduled time with backoff on failure, then update status.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["Create Job"] --> B[(Jobs table)]
    B --> C[(Executions table)]
    C --> D["Scheduler scan window"]
    D --> E["Delay queue"]
    E --> F["Worker executes"]
    F --> G["Update status"]

scenario: 创建请求返回 200 后进程可能立刻崩溃，落库的那行必须表明这个 Job 还没跑过。
scenario_en: The process can crash right after the create call returns 200, so the stored row must show the job has not run yet.
q: Job 刚被创建、写入数据库时，初始状态应是什么？
q_en: When a job is first created and written to the database, what should its initial status be?
options: COMPLETED
IN_PROGRESS
PENDING
FAILED
why: 新 Job 以 PENDING 落库，好处是有持久记录、崩溃可恢复、可全生命周期追踪状态。
why_en: A newly created job is persisted with status PENDING so it has a durable, recoverable record.
options_en: COMPLETED
IN_PROGRESS
PENDING
FAILED
optionExplanations: 这是执行完成后的终态，刚创建的 Job 还没跑，不可能是这个状态。
这是正在执行中的状态，Job 刚落库时还没被 Worker 领取，不该是这个。
对，PENDING 表示已落库、还没开始执行，是新 Job 唯一合理的起点。
这是失败终态，Job 都还没跑过，谈不上失败。
optionExplanations_en: That's the terminal state after a run finishes — a brand-new job hasn't run yet, so it can't start there.
That means a worker is already running it — a job that just got written to the DB hasn't been picked up yet.
Right: PENDING means it's persisted but not yet started — the only sane starting point for a new job.
That's a terminal failure state — the job hasn't even run once, so it can't already be failed.

scenario: 10k/s 的 Job 若只留在内存，Scheduler 一次重启就全丢；面试官问持久化换来什么。
scenario_en: If 10k jobs per second lived only in memory, one scheduler restart would lose them all; what does persistence buy you?
q: 把 Job 先持久化到数据库（而非只留在内存）带来了哪些好处？（多选）
q_en: What benefits come from persisting a job to the database instead of keeping it only in memory? (select all)
options: 拥有所有 Job 的持久记录
系统崩溃后能恢复未完成的 Job
能在整个生命周期追踪 Job 状态
无需任何 Worker 即可自动执行
why: 持久化换来记录、崩溃恢复和状态追踪三重好处；但执行仍需 Worker，持久化本身不会执行 Job。
why_en: Persisting jobs gives a durable record, crash recovery, and status tracking, but execution still needs workers.
options_en: It gives a durable record of every job.
The system can recover unfinished jobs after a crash.
Job status can be tracked across its whole lifecycle.
No worker is needed at all; jobs execute automatically.
optionExplanations: 对，落库之后每个 Job 都有正式记录，不再只活在某个进程的内存里。
对，进程崩溃时内存里的东西全丢，但数据库里的 Job 还在，能接着恢复。
对，状态能在 PENDING→执行中→完成/失败这条链路上被持续追踪。
错，落库只是留了个记录，真正把代码跑起来仍然要靠 Worker 去执行。
optionExplanations_en: Right: once persisted, every job has a real record instead of living only in one process's memory.
Right: a crash wipes in-memory state, but the database copy survives, so recovery is possible.
Right: status can be tracked continuously through pending, running, and done or failed.
Wrong: persisting just leaves a record — actually running the code still needs a worker.

scenario: Job 数据关系少、不需要强一致、要方便日后水平扩展到 10k/s，面试官不限定技术栈。
scenario_en: Job data has few relationships, doesn't need strong consistency, and must scale horizontally to 10k/s later; the interviewer leaves the tech stack open.
q: 作者默认选用的数据库是？
q_en: Which database does the author default to?
options: 单实例部署的 Postgres 关系型主库，靠强一致换取简单的 join 查询
灵活的键值存储 DynamoDB（或 Cassandra）
专门存储节点和边关系的 Neo4j 图数据库，适合复杂关系遍历
面向全文检索和聚合分析的 Elasticsearch 搜索引擎，不适合当主存储
why: 数据关系少、无强一致需求、要好扩展，因此选 DynamoDB 这类键值存储（开源偏好则 Cassandra）。Postgres/MySQL 也能用，只是后期扩展要多费心。
why_en: With few relationships, no strong-consistency need, and easy scaling, a key-value store like DynamoDB or Cassandra is the default.
whenOtherWins: 如果数据高度关系化、需要多表事务和强一致，或团队只用开源关系库，Postgres/MySQL 更合适（代价是扩展要额外下功夫）。
tradeoff: 易扩展的键值存储 vs 关系型数据库的强一致与多表能力
options_en: A single-instance, single-primary Postgres relational database, trading scale for strong consistency and easy joins.
A flexible key-value store like DynamoDB (or Cassandra).
The Neo4j graph database, built to store nodes and their relationships, good for complex relationship traversal.
The Elasticsearch search engine, built for full-text search and aggregation, not a fit as the primary store.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管键值/文档数据库，按分区键分散读写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed AWS key-value and document database that spreads reads and writes by partition key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源的分布式宽列存储数据库，强调高可用与横向扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is an open-source distributed wide-column database built for high availability and horizontal scale.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门存储节点和边关系的图数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Neo4j is a graph database built to store nodes and their relationships.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向全文检索和聚合分析的搜索引擎。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is a search engine built for full-text search and aggregation.

optionExplanations: 数据高度关系化、要多表事务或强一致时更该选它，但这里关系少、要横向扩到大规模。
对，数据关系少、不追求强一致、又要扩到万级 QPS，键值存储的水平扩展天然合适。
图数据库擅长的是节点和边的关系遍历，这里根本没有那种图状数据。
全文检索引擎解决的是搜索排序问题，Job 调度不需要对文本做相关性检索。
optionExplanations_en: That fits when data is highly relational and you need multi-table transactions or strong consistency — this scenario has neither.
Right: with few relations, no strong-consistency need, and a target of tens of thousands of QPS, a key-value store's horizontal scaling fits directly.
Graph databases shine at traversing nodes and edges — there's no graph-shaped data here at all.
A search engine is built for relevance ranking over text — job scheduling has no text search need.

scenario: 单张 Jobs 表直接存 CRON 表达式，而系统每隔几秒就要找出「接下来几分钟到期的 Job」。
scenario_en: One Jobs table stores raw CRON expressions, yet every few seconds the system must find the jobs due in the next few minutes.
q: 把所有信息塞进单张 Jobs 表、直接存 CRON 表达式，会遇到什么根本问题？
q_en: What's the fundamental problem with cramming everything into one Jobs table and storing the raw CRON expression?
options: 这种单表设计根本无法把 parameters 参数存成 JSON 格式来使用
要找出「接下来几分钟该跑的 Job」，得扫描并求值每一条 CRON 表达式，无法扩展
这种设计里 user_id 这个字段完全没有办法被记录保存下来
一次性 Job（只用具体 DateTime 而非 CRON）在这种设计里也没法被存储
why: 单表存 CRON 时，找「即将执行的 Job」必须遍历求值所有 CRON 表达式，随数据量线性膨胀，不可扩展。这逼出「定义与执行实例分离」。
why_en: Storing CRON in one table forces evaluating every expression to find upcoming jobs, which does not scale.
options_en: This single-table design cannot store the parameters field as JSON at all.
Finding upcoming jobs means evaluating every CRON expression, which does not scale.
In this design, the user_id field has no way to be recorded at all.
One-time jobs, which use a specific DateTime instead of CRON, cannot be stored in this design either.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用固定语法表示周期性时间规则的表达式，如「每天 10 点」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CRON expression is a fixed syntax for describing a recurring schedule, like every day at ten.

optionExplanations: JSON 字段本来就能正常存参数，这不是这种单表设计真正的痛点。
对，找『接下来要跑的 Job』得挨个求值每条 CRON，数据一多就线性拖垮查询。
user_id 只是普通字段，单表里存它完全没问题。
一次性 Job 用具体 DateTime 存本来就没障碍，跟 CRON 是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: A JSON column can store parameters just fine — that's not the real pain point of this layout.
Right: finding what's due soon means evaluating every CRON expression one by one, and that scales linearly with the table's size.
user_id is just an ordinary column — storing it in a single table is no problem at all.
One-time jobs stored with a plain DateTime were never blocked — that's a separate concern from CRON.

scenario: 需要支持周期性 Job（如每天 10 点），又要能高效查出「即将要跑的实例」。
scenario_en: The design must support recurring jobs (like every day at 10am) while still efficiently finding the instances that are about to run.
q: 关键设计洞见是什么？
q_en: What's the key design insight here?
options: 把 CRON 求值放到应用层缓存里，缓存一旦失效仍要重新遍历求值所有表达式
把 Job 的「定义」与它的「执行实例」拆成两张表
给 CRON 表达式建全文索引
改用关系数据库做多表 join
why: 核心洞见：分离「定义」与「执行实例」——像日历里「每周一重复的事件」会展开成一个个具体周一的实例。Jobs 表存定义，Executions 表存每次执行。
why_en: The key insight is separating the job definition from its execution instances, like a calendar expands a recurring event into individual occurrences.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有纯一次性 Job、永不周期，单表其实够用；分离主要是为周期性和高效查询服务。
diagram:
flowchart TD
    J["Job definition"] --> S["Schedule rule"]
    S --> E1["Execution 10:00"]
    S --> E2["Execution 10:05"]
    S --> E3["Execution 10:10"]
    E1 --> H["status history"]
    E2 --> H
    E3 --> H
tradeoff: 定义/实例分离（可扩展查询） vs 单表存储（简单但需遍历求值）
options_en: Cache CRON evaluation results at the application layer., and once the cache goes stale you're back to re-evaluating everything.
Split the job definition and its execution instances into two tables.
Build a full-text index on the CRON expressions.
Switch to a relational database with multi-table joins.
optionExplanations: 把求值结果缓存住只是暂时止痛，Job 一多、缓存一失效，还是得重新扫一遍。
对，把『定义』和『执行实例』拆成两张表，查询就能只看即将发生的实例，不用扫定义。
全文索引是给文本相关性排序用的，CRON 表达式不是要被『搜索』的文本。
换关系库做多表 join 没有解决『要遍历求值 CRON』这个根本问题，只是换了个数据库。
optionExplanations_en: Caching the evaluated result only delays the pain — once jobs grow or the cache goes stale, you're back to rescanning everything.
Right: splitting definition from execution instance lets a query look only at upcoming instances, without ever scanning definitions.
Full-text indexing is for ranking text relevance — a CRON expression isn't something you search for.
Switching to a relational database with joins doesn't remove the need to evaluate every CRON — it just moves the same problem.

scenario: Jobs 表要承接 10k/s 的写入，落在 DynamoDB 的多个分区上，不能让任何单分区被写爆。
scenario_en: The Jobs table absorbs 10k writes per second across DynamoDB partitions, and no single partition may become a write hotspot.
q: Jobs 表（存 Job 定义）用什么作分区键（partition key）？
q_en: What's used as the partition key for the Jobs table (which stores job definitions)?
options: user_id（同一用户的 Job 会挤到同一个分区）
job_id（每个 Job 唯一，写入天然分散）
time_bucket（这其实是 Executions 表用的分区键）
task_id（同一个 Task 常被多个 Job 复用）
why: Jobs 表用 job_id 作分区键，每个 Job 唯一 → 写入均匀分散到各分区，天然避免热点。
why_en: The Jobs table is partitioned by job_id, whose uniqueness spreads writes evenly across partitions.
options_en: user_id, which would crowd one user's jobs onto a single partition.
job_id, unique per job, so writes spread evenly
time_bucket, which is actually the partition key used by the Executions table.
task_id, which the same task often reuses across many jobs.
optionExplanations: 按 user_id 分区会让活跃用户的 Job 全挤进同一个分区，制造热点而不是分散。
对，job_id 天生唯一，用它做分区键能让写入自然均匀分散，不制造热点。
这其实是 Executions 表用的分区键，用在 Jobs 表上会挤爆当前时间那个分区。
同一个 Task 常被很多 Job 复用，按 task_id 分区一样会把写入堆到少数几个分区。
optionExplanations_en: Partitioning by user_id would pile an active user's jobs into one partition — that creates a hotspot instead of spreading writes.
Right: job_id is unique by nature, so partitioning on it spreads writes evenly with no hotspot.
That's actually the Executions table's partition key — reusing it here would jam everything into the current time bucket.
A single task gets reused by many jobs, so partitioning by task_id would still pile writes onto a handful of partitions.

scenario: Executions 表的主查询是「取出某个小时窗口内到期的执行实例」，同一 Job 会重复执行多次。
scenario_en: The Executions table's main query pulls instances due inside an hour window, and the same job runs many times over.
q: Executions 表的复合主键设计是怎样的？
q_en: What is the composite primary key design for the Executions table?
options: 分区键选 job_id，排序键选 status，同一 Job 多次执行会互相覆盖
分区键 time_bucket，排序键 execution_time+job_id
分区键选 user_id，排序键选 attempt，图的是按用户批量查询方便
只用 job_id 一个字段作单一主键，完全不设置排序键，图省事但丢了区分执行批次的能力
why: Executions 表用 time_bucket（按小时向下取整的时间戳）作分区键，execution_time + job_id 作排序键保证复合主键唯一，便于按时间窗口查询。
why_en: The Executions table uses an hourly time_bucket as partition key and execution_time plus job_id as the unique sort key.
options_en: Partition key job_id, sort key status; repeated runs of the same job would overwrite each other.
Partition key time_bucket, sort key execution_time plus job_id.
Partition key user_id, sort key attempt, aimed at making per-user lookups fast.
A single primary key of just job_id, no sort key at all — simple, but it loses the ability to tell attempts apart.
optionExplanations: job_id 做分区键更适合 Jobs 表；status 也不能保证唯一，同一个 Job 的多次执行会互相覆盖。
对，time_bucket 分区把同一小时的执行聚在一起，execution_time+job_id 保证同分区内主键唯一。
user_id 分区服务的是『按用户查』这条次要路径，不是『找即将执行的 Job』这条主路径。
只用 job_id 当主键，图省事，但和第一个选项一个毛病：没有排序键区分执行批次，没法知道是哪一次。
optionExplanations_en: job_id as a partition key belongs to the Jobs table, and status alone can't guarantee uniqueness — repeated runs of the same job would overwrite each other.
Right: partitioning by time_bucket groups an hour's executions together, and execution_time plus job_id keeps the key unique within it.
Partitioning by user_id serves the secondary 'look up by user' path, not the primary 'find what's due soon' one.
Using only job_id as the key is simple to set up, but it has the same problem as the first option: no sort key to distinguish attempts, so there's no way to tell which run is which.

scenario: Executions 表用 time_bucket 做分区键，需要把任意一个执行时间戳映射到它所在的那个小时。
scenario_en: The Executions table partitions by time_bucket, so any execution timestamp must map to the hour it falls into.
q: 补全 time_bucket 的计算方式：
q_en: Fill in how time_bucket is computed:
text: time_bucket = (execution_time // {{3600}}) * {{3600}}，即把执行时间向下取整到最近的{{小时}}。
why: 按小时取整生成 time_bucket 作分区键，使得查「即将执行的 Job」只需扫当前小时（可能加下一小时）这 1-2 个分区。
why_en: The time bucket rounds the execution time down to the nearest hour by integer-dividing by 3600 and multiplying back.

scenario: Scheduler 每隔几秒问一次「接下来该跑哪些 Job」，扫的分区越少这次查询越快。
scenario_en: Every few seconds the scheduler asks which jobs are due next, and the fewer partitions it scans the faster that query returns.
q: 用「按小时取整的 time_bucket」作分区键，最大好处是什么？
q_en: What's the biggest benefit of using an hour-rounded time_bucket as the partition key?
options: 这种取整方式据说能够彻底消除任何形式的热点分区问题
查「即将执行的 Job」只需查 1-2 个分区（当前小时 + 可能下一小时）
这样的分区设计能够让 Job 的定义从此永远不会重复出现
这种分区键的设计方式能够自动实现 Job 失败后的重试逻辑，还顺带优化了写入吞吐和索引占用
why: time_bucket 把同一小时的执行聚到一个分区，查即将执行的 Job 只需扫 1-2 个分区，读非常高效。代价是可能形成热分区，后面用写分片解决。
why_en: The hourly time bucket lets us query only one or two partitions to find all upcoming jobs, giving very efficient reads.
options_en: This rounding scheme supposedly eliminates any form of hot partition entirely.
Finding upcoming jobs needs only one or two partitions.
This partitioning design supposedly makes job definitions never repeat again.
This partition-key design supposedly automatically implements retry logic after a job fails., and supposedly optimizes write throughput and indexing along the way.
optionExplanations: 恰恰相反，把同一小时全砸进一个分区，反而是制造热点的根源，不是消除它。
对，即将执行的 Job 都挤在当前（和下一）小时桶里，扫 1-2 个分区就能查全。
分区键管的是数据物理分布，跟『Job 定义会不会重复』完全是两件事。
分区键只决定数据存哪，重试逻辑得靠 Worker 和队列自己实现，不会自动生成。
optionExplanations_en: It's actually the opposite — jamming a whole hour into one partition is what creates the hotspot, not what removes it.
Right: everything due soon sits in the current (and maybe next) hour's bucket, so 1-2 partitions cover the whole query.
The partition key governs physical data placement — it has nothing to do with whether job definitions repeat.
A partition key only decides where data lives; retry logic still has to be built in the worker and queue, not conjured automatically.

scenario: 峰值 10k Job/s 的写入，全部落到同一个小时的那一个 time_bucket 分区上。
scenario_en: At peak, 10k job writes per second all land in the single time_bucket partition for the current hour.
q: 把某一小时的所有写入集中到同一个分区，潜在风险是什么？
q_en: What's the risk of concentrating an entire hour's writes into a single partition?
options: 会导致该时间桶下的读取查询明显变慢，拖慢 Worker 拉取速度
重负载下可能形成热分区（hot partition）
会导致这套设计完全无法支持周期性 Job 的重复调度
会导致写入记录里的 job_id 字段丢失，后续没法追溯
why: 当前小时所有写入落到同一分区，高负载下会成热分区。作者在扩展深潜里用「写分片」（给分区键加随机后缀）来分摊。
why_en: Concentrating an hour's writes into one partition risks a hot partition under heavy load, addressed later with write sharding.
options_en: It would make read queries against that time bucket noticeably slower, slowing down worker pull rates.
Under heavy load it can create a hot partition.
It would make this design completely unable to support recurring jobs' repeat scheduling.
It would cause the job_id field to be lost from written records, making runs untraceable afterward.
optionExplanations: 读取确实可能被拖慢，但根源在写入全砸向一个分区，先烧穿的是写吞吐上限，不是这条读延迟。
对，一小时的写入全砸向同一个分区，负载一高就会撞到分区写容量上限。
热分区是性能问题，不会让周期性 Job 这个功能直接失效。
热分区影响的是写入能不能扛住，不会凭空把已经写进去的字段丢掉。
optionExplanations_en: Reads can get dragged down too, but the root cause is writes all hammering one partition first, not this read-latency story.
Right: a whole hour's writes land on the same partition, so heavy load runs straight into that partition's write ceiling.
A hot partition is a performance problem — it doesn't disable the periodic-job feature itself.
A hot partition affects whether writes keep up — it doesn't make an already-written field disappear.

scenario: 「每天 10 点发报表」这个 Job 刚跑完一次，定义不变，但明天那次必须被安排上。
scenario_en: The daily 10am report job just finished a run; its definition is unchanged but tomorrow's run still has to get scheduled.
q: 在「定义 / 执行实例分离」下，周期性 Job 完成一次后如何安排下一次？
q_en: Under the definition-versus-execution-instance split, how is the next run of a recurring job scheduled after one completes?
options: 直接修改 Job 定义表里记录下一次调度时间的字段数值，省了插入新记录这一步
保持 Job 定义不变，计算下一次执行时间并在 Executions 表插入一条新实例
把整张 Jobs 定义表原封不动地复制一份、另存成一条新记录，图的是保留历史
先彻底删除这个旧的 Job 定义记录，再重新创建一个全新的 Job 出来，等于换了个调度对象
why: 周期性 Job 完成后，定义（Jobs 表）不动，只按计划算出下次时间、在 Executions 表插入新执行实例。不断生成新实例即可支持重复。
why_en: For recurring jobs the definition stays fixed while a new execution instance is inserted for the next computed run time.
options_en: Directly edit the time field in the job definition that records the next scheduled time, skipping the insert step.
Keep the definition unchanged and insert a new Executions row.
Copy the entire Jobs definition table as-is and save it as another new record, aiming to keep history around.
First fully delete the old job definition, then create a brand-new job from scratch — effectively a different scheduled object.
optionExplanations: Job 定义里根本没有『下一次时间』这种可变字段，这套设计压根不改定义，也没有『插入』这一步可省。
对，Jobs 表里那条定义完全不碰，只是把下次该跑的时间点重新算一遍，写成一条新的执行记录，靠这个循环支持重复。
复制整张定义表既没必要，也违背『定义只保留一份、被反复复用』的设计初衷，历史该由 Executions 表来存。
删了再建等于换了个新 Job，和『同一个周期性 Job 持续产生新实例』完全是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: The job definition doesn't even have a mutable 'next time' field — this design never touches the definition, so there's no insert step to skip.
Right: the definition stays untouched, and the next occurrence just becomes a new row inserted into Executions.
Copying the whole definition row is both unnecessary and defeats the point of keeping one reusable definition — history belongs in the Executions table.
Deleting and recreating is effectively a different job — that's not the same as one recurring job spawning new instances.

scenario: 面试官问这套「定义表 + 执行实例表」的拆法，还能迁移到哪些同样有重复行为的系统。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks which other systems with repeating behavior can reuse this definition-table-plus-instance-table split.
q: 「把定义与实例分离」这一模式还常见于哪些系统？（多选）
q_en: Where else does the definition-versus-instance pattern commonly show up? (select all)
options: 日历系统：事件定义 vs 每次发生的实例
通知系统：模板 vs 单条通知
任务调度：Job 定义 vs 执行记录
负载均衡器分配请求
why: 定义 vs 实例是通用模式：日历（事件 vs 每次发生）、通知（模板 vs 单条）、调度（定义 vs 执行），处理重复 / 模板化行为很有力。
why_en: Separating template from instance appears in calendars, notifications, and schedulers alike.
options_en: Calendars: an event definition versus each occurrence.
Notifications: a template versus an individual notification.
Job scheduling: a job definition versus its execution records.
A load balancer distributing requests.
optionExplanations: 对，日历里『每周一重复的会议』是定义，某个具体周一发生的那次是实例。
对，通知模板是定义，发给某个用户的那一条具体通知是实例。
对，这正是本题在做的事：Job 定义 vs Executions 里的每次执行实例。
负载均衡器转发请求走的是路由算法，不涉及『定义 vs 反复发生的实例』这种模式。
optionExplanations_en: Right: a calendar's 'recurring Monday meeting' is the definition, and one specific Monday's occurrence is the instance.
Right: a notification template is the definition, and the one message sent to a user is the instance.
Right: that's exactly what this system does — a job definition versus each execution instance.
A load balancer routes requests using a routing algorithm — that's unrelated to a definition-versus-recurring-instance pattern.

q: 补全 Worker 拉取待执行 Job 的查询条件：
q_en: Fill in the query conditions a worker uses to pull due jobs:
text: Worker 查询 Executions 表：execution_time 落在接下来几分钟、且 status 为 {{PENDING}}；再去 {{Jobs}} 表按 job_id 查出完整定义后执行。
why: Worker 从 Executions 表按时间窗口 + PENDING 状态取出待跑实例，再回 Jobs 表取完整任务定义和参数来执行。
why_en: Workers query the Executions table for imminent PENDING entries, then look up full details in the Jobs table to execute.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    W["Worker"] --> Q["Query bucket"]
    Q --> F["scheduled_at <= now"]
    F --> P["status = pending"]
    P --> C["claim execution"]
    C --> R["run job"]

scenario: 监控页要让用户看到一个 Job 从落库到最终成功或失败的整个过程，中间还可能重试。
scenario_en: The monitoring page must show a job's whole path from insert to eventual success or failure, retries included.
q: Job 执行过程中，Executions 表的 status 字段可能取哪些值？（多选）
q_en: During a job's execution, what values can the Executions table's status field take? (select all)
options: COMPLETED（完成）
FAILED（失败）
IN_PROGRESS / RETRYING（执行中 / 重试中）
PENDING（待执行）
why: 状态在生命周期内流转：PENDING → IN_PROGRESS →（RETRYING）→ COMPLETED / FAILED，供监控查询。
why_en: Execution status flows through PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, RETRYING, COMPLETED, and FAILED.
options_en: COMPLETED
FAILED
IN_PROGRESS / RETRYING
PENDING
optionExplanations: 对，任务代码顺利跑完就落在这个终态。
对，代码抛异常或重试次数耗尽后，最终落在这个终态。
对，Worker 正在处理、或失败后带着退避在等下一次尝试，都算这个中间态。
对，Execution 实例刚生成、还没被任何 Worker 领取时的起始态。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the terminal state once the task code finishes successfully.
Right: the terminal state once the code throws or retries run out.
Right: the in-between state, covering both a worker actively running it and a backoff wait before the next retry.
Right: the starting state right after an execution instance is created, before any worker has picked it up.

scenario: 监控页要「列出某用户的全部 Job 及状态」，但表的主键只按 time_bucket 组织。
scenario_en: The monitoring page must list all of one user's jobs with statuses, but the table key is organized only by time_bucket.
q: 在只有 time_bucket 分区键的原设计下，「按 user_id 查某用户所有 Job」为什么低效？
q_en: In the original design keyed only by time_bucket, why is querying all of a user's jobs by user_id inefficient?
options: user_id 这个字段其实从一开始就根本没有被存储下来，所以无论怎么查都不可能按用户做任何形式的过滤
需要先全表扫描 Jobs 找出该用户的所有 job_id，再逐个查 Executions 状态
DynamoDB 这类数据库天生就不支持按用户维度做查询
这种查询方式执行时会直接阻塞住系统里的所有写入操作
why: 主键按 time_bucket 组织，按用户查得先全表扫 Jobs 表找 job_id，再逐个查 Executions，两步都低效。需要为用户访问模式建索引。
why_en: Without a user-oriented index, querying by user needs a full scan of Jobs then per-job Executions lookups.
options_en: The user_id field was actually never stored in the first place., so no user-scoped filtering would ever be possible at all.
It needs a full Jobs scan, then a per-job Executions lookup.
DynamoDB-style databases inherently cannot support querying by user at all.
Running this kind of query would directly block every write operation in the system.
optionExplanations: user_id 一直都好好存在字段里，问题不在存没存，而在怎么查。
对，扫描代价 ≈ Jobs 表总行数（不是这一个用户的 Job 数），后面还得一条条去核对执行记录，成本雪上加霜。
DynamoDB 能按任意字段查，只是没建索引时那次查询效率很差，不是数据库能力的限制。
全表扫描是读操作，拖慢的是读延迟，不会把写入通道堵死。
optionExplanations_en: user_id was stored fine all along — the problem isn't whether it exists, it's how you query it.
Right: the scan cost is roughly the whole Jobs table's row count, not this one user's job count, and querying Executions one by one on top makes it worse.
DynamoDB can filter on any field — it's just slow without an index, not a hard limitation of the database itself.
A full table scan is a read; it slows down reads, it doesn't block the write path.

scenario: 要高效支持「查某用户的所有执行、按时间排序、可分页、可按状态过滤」，同时不破坏主访问模式（找即将执行的 Job）。
scenario_en: The design must efficiently support querying all of a user's executions, sorted by time, paginated, and filterable by status, without disturbing the primary access pattern of finding upcoming jobs.
q: 最合适的做法是？
q_en: What's the best approach?
options: 在 Executions 表建 GSI：按 user_id 查询
把整张 Executions 表按 user_id 重新分区
每次查询都全表扫描
把用户数据复制到单独的 Postgres
why: 在 Executions 表加 GSI（分区键 user_id、排序键 execution_time+job_id），即可高效按用户查、按时间排序、分页、按状态过滤，且不动主访问模式。
why_en: A GSI keyed on user_id with an execution_time sort key efficiently serves user queries without disturbing the primary access pattern.
whenOtherWins: 如果按用户查是极低频的分析需求，也可离线导出到数仓再查，省下 GSI 的写开销和成本。
tradeoff: 加 GSI 服务用户维度查询 vs 保持主表只按 time_bucket 访问
options_en: Add a GSI on the Executions table keyed by user_id.
Re-partition the entire Executions table by user_id.
Do a full table scan on every query.
Copy user data into a separate Postgres instance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全局二级索引，让 DynamoDB 表支持主键之外的额外查询模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI, or global secondary index, lets a DynamoDB table serve queries beyond its primary key.

optionExplanations: 对，加一个 GSI，写放大 ≈ 多一次索引写，换来按用户查询不用碰主访问路径。
把整张表按 user_id 重新分区，会直接打乱『按时间桶找即将执行 Job』这条主路径。
全表扫描没有利用任何索引，用户一多、数据一大就直接查不动。
为了一个查询维度专门搭一套 Postgres 同步，运维成本远超加一个 GSI。
optionExplanations_en: Right: adding a GSI costs roughly one extra index write per write, in exchange for a user-scoped query that never touches the main access path.
Re-partitioning the whole table by user_id would break the primary 'find what's due by time bucket' path outright.
A full scan uses no index at all — it stops being workable the moment users or data grow.
Standing up a whole separate Postgres just for one query shape costs far more ops overhead than a single GSI.

scenario: 已经在 Executions 表上加了一个按 user_id 查询的全局二级索引（GSI），用来服务用户查看自己 Job 的场景。
scenario_en: A global secondary index (GSI) keyed on user_id has been added to the Executions table to serve users viewing their own jobs.
q: 为用户查询加 GSI 的主要代价是什么？
q_en: What's the main cost of adding this GSI for user queries?
options: 加 GSI 会彻底破坏原来那条按 time_bucket 查询的主访问路径
增加一些写开销和成本，但换来高效的用户维度查询，值得
加了这个 GSI 之后会直接导致 Job 完全无法被执行
加了 GSI 会让读取变得不一致到几乎不可用的地步
why: GSI 会带来额外写入开销和成本，但相比在基表里冗余 user_id、让数据模型更复杂，用 GSI 维护多访问模式更划算。
why_en: The GSI adds some write overhead and cost, but it is a worthwhile trade-off for efficient user-side queries.
options_en: Adding the GSI would completely break the original time_bucket-based primary access path.
It adds some write overhead and cost, but the trade-off is worth it.
Adding this GSI would directly make jobs completely unable to execute.
Adding the GSI would make reads inconsistent to the point of being nearly unusable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全局二级索引，让 DynamoDB 表支持主键之外的额外查询模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI, or global secondary index, lets a DynamoDB table serve queries beyond its primary key.

optionExplanations: GSI 和基表的主访问路径互不干扰，加了它并不会破坏按 time_bucket 查询。
对，多一份索引写入确实要花成本，但换来高效的用户维度查询，这笔账划算。
GSI 只是多加一条查询路径，跟 Job 能不能被执行没有任何关系。
GSI 本身遵循基表的一致性模型，不会把读取拖到不可用的地步。
optionExplanations_en: A GSI doesn't interfere with the base table's main access path — adding one doesn't break the time_bucket query.
Right: the extra index write does cost something, but it buys efficient user-scoped queries, and that trade is worth it.
A GSI just adds another query path — it has nothing to do with whether jobs can execute.
A GSI inherits the base table's consistency model — it doesn't drag reads down to unusable.

scenario: 非功能需求要求 Job 在调度时间 2 秒内执行，而朴素方案是每 2 分钟轮询一次数据库。
scenario_en: The requirement is that jobs run within two seconds of their scheduled time, while the naive design polls the database every two minutes.
q: 「每隔几分钟轮询数据库找待执行 Job」为什么无法满足 2 秒精度？
q_en: Why can polling the database every few minutes for due jobs never meet a two-second precision target?
options: 是因为数据库本身根本不支持任何时间范围相关的查询
轮询周期本身就是执行精度的上界：每 2 分钟轮询，Job 就可能早/晚 2 分钟
是因为部署的 Worker 实例数量本身就完全不够用
是因为 CRON 表达式这种语法格式根本没办法被正确解析，跟查询数据库的频率完全无关
why: 轮询频率天然是精度上界：每 2 分钟查一次，Job 最多可能偏差 2 分钟。要 2 秒精度就得每 2 秒查一次，但那样代价太大。
why_en: The polling interval is itself the upper bound on precision, so minute-level polling means minute-level error.
options_en: Because the database itself does not support any time-range queries at all.
The polling interval is itself the upper bound on precision.
Because the number of deployed worker instances is simply not enough.
Because CRON expressions as a syntax simply cannot be parsed correctly., which has nothing to do with how often the database gets queried.
optionExplanations: 数据库本身完全能做时间范围查询，问题从来不是查询能力，而是多久查一次。
对，查询频率就是精度天花板：2 分钟一轮，Job 最坏就可能偏差 2 分钟。
就算加再多 Worker，还没到轮询那一刻，Job 也压根不会被取出来执行。
CRON 只是决定生成哪些执行实例，解析它跟『多久扫一次库』毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: The database can absolutely do time-range queries — the issue was never query capability, it's how often you query.
Right: the polling frequency is the precision ceiling — every 2 minutes means up to 2 minutes of possible drift.
More worker instances wouldn't help — until the next poll fires, the job simply hasn't been pulled out to run yet.
CRON only decides which execution instances get generated; parsing it has nothing to do with how often you scan the database.

scenario: 为凑 2 秒精度把轮询改成每 2 秒一次，而峰值 10k Job/s 意味着每次约 2 万条到期。
scenario_en: To chase two-second precision you poll every two seconds, but at 10k jobs per second that's about 20,000 due rows each round.
q: 「干脆把轮询频率提到每 2 秒一次」为什么不可行？（多选）
q_en: Why is simply bumping the polling frequency to every two seconds not workable? (select all)
options: 10k/s 下每次要取处理约 2 万个 Job，负载巨大
即使有索引，查 2 万条也要几百毫秒，加网络和序列化可能 500ms
取回后还要初始化、分发给 Worker、启动执行，进一步吃掉精度窗口
每 2 秒的大查询给数据库巨大压力，影响其他操作和稳定性
why: 高频大查询四宗罪：单次约 2 万 Job 的大负载、查询本身几百 ms、分发执行的额外开销、以及持续压垮数据库。所以要换两层架构。
why_en: Polling every two seconds fails due to huge per-query payloads, hundreds of milliseconds of query time, distribution overhead, and heavy database load.
options_en: At ten thousand jobs per second, each query would fetch about twenty thousand due jobs, a huge payload.
Even with indexing, scanning twenty thousand rows plus network and serialization could take about 500ms.
After fetching, distributing jobs to workers and starting execution eats further into the precision window.
Running such large queries every two seconds would put heavy, destabilizing load on the database.
optionExplanations: 对，10k/s 乘以 2 秒窗口，一次就要捞出约 2 万条待办 Job，单批负载就不小。
对，就算有索引，2 万条查询加上网络和序列化，累计也可能到几百毫秒。
对，取回之后还要初始化任务、分发给 Worker、再启动执行，这几步继续吃掉本就紧张的窗口。
对，每 2 秒一次的大查询会持续占用数据库资源，连带拖慢其他读写操作。
optionExplanations_en: Right: at 10k/s over a 2-second window, one fetch pulls roughly 20,000 due jobs — that's already a heavy single batch.
Right: even with an index, querying 20,000 rows plus network and serialization can add up to several hundred milliseconds.
Right: after the fetch, initializing, dispatching to workers, and starting execution eat further into an already tight window.
Right: a heavy query every 2 seconds keeps the database busy and drags down other reads and writes alongside it.

q: 把「两层调度架构」的完整流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the full flow of the two-layer scheduler architecture:
steps: Worker 持续轮询 SQS，消息到点变可见即被处理执行
用户创建 Job，写入数据库
Cron 把这批 Job 带上合适的 delay 发到 SQS
Cron 每 5 分钟查数据库，取出接下来约 5 分钟要执行的 Job
why: 两层架构：写库 → cron 每 5 分钟捞出未来 5 分钟的 Job → 带 delay 推入 SQS → Worker 持续拉取、到点执行。数据库低频查、队列保精度。
why_en: The two-layer scheduler writes to the database, a five-minute cron pulls upcoming jobs into SQS with delays, and workers poll SQS to execute on time.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    U["用户创建 Job"] --> DB[("数据库")]
    DB --> C["Cron 每 5 分钟查询"]
    C --> Q["SQS 延迟队列"]
    Q --> W["Worker 拉取执行"]

scenario: 要同时兼顾「数据库不被高频查询压垮」和「Job 能按秒级精度执行」。
scenario_en: The design must keep the database from being overwhelmed by high-frequency queries while still executing jobs with second-level precision.
q: 两层调度架构如何同时满足这两点？
q_en: How does the two-layer scheduler architecture satisfy both at once?
options: 让 Worker 直接每秒查数据库，图的是实现简单不用引入队列
查库低频（5 分钟一次），队列缓冲保证高吞吐执行
把所有 Job 缓存在应用内存里轮询，省去数据库查询延迟
取消数据库，全部用 Redis 做持久化和调度
why: 两层解耦「查库」与「执行」：数据库每 5 分钟才查一次（低负载），消息队列高吞吐让 Worker 一到点就能拉取执行（保精度），去掉了执行频率的上界。
why_en: Splitting database querying from execution lets the database run infrequent queries while the queue delivers jobs at high throughput for precise execution.
whenOtherWins: 如果精度要求很松（比如分钟级即可）且规模很小，单层定期轮询更简单，无需引入队列。
tradeoff: 数据库低频查询 vs 队列保精度、高吞吐
options_en: Have workers query the database every second directly, aiming for simplicity by skipping the queue.
Query the database infrequently while a queue buffers jobs for high-throughput execution.
Cache every job in application memory and poll it, avoiding database query latency.
Remove the database entirely and use only Redis for persistence and scheduling.
optionExplanations: Worker 直接每秒查库，等于把高频查询压力原样转嫁给数据库，没有解耦。
对，数据库低频查（5 分钟一次）减轻负载，队列负责高吞吐分发，两层各司其职。
把全部 Job 缓存进单进程内存，既没有持久化也扛不住多实例横向扩展。
扔掉数据库，Job 定义和历史记录就没地方持久存放，崩溃也没法恢复。
optionExplanations_en: Workers hitting the database every second just shifts the high-frequency load onto it directly — nothing gets decoupled.
Right: the database is polled infrequently (every 5 minutes) to cut load, while the queue handles high-throughput delivery — each layer does its own job.
Caching every job in one process's memory has no durability and can't scale across multiple instances.
Dropping the database leaves nowhere durable to store job definitions and history, and nothing to recover from after a crash.

scenario: 两层调度架构里，第一层负责定期把即将到期的 Job 从数据库捞出来，再送进延迟队列。
scenario_en: In the two-layer scheduler, the first layer periodically pulls soon-due jobs from the database and hands them to the delay queue.
q: 两层架构里，第一层 cron 每隔多久查一次数据库、取出未来多久内的 Job？
q_en: In the two-layer architecture, how often does the first-layer cron query the database, and how far ahead does it fetch jobs?
options: 每 2 秒查一次数据库，只取未来 2 秒内到期的 Job
每 5 分钟查一次，取未来约 5 分钟（留网络延迟缓冲）
每小时查一次数据库，取出未来整整 1 小时内的 Job
每天只查一次数据库，取出当天全部要执行的 Job
why: cron 每 5 分钟查一次，取出未来约 5 分钟内到期的 Job（留些缓冲应对网络延迟），大幅降低数据库负载。
why_en: The cron runs every five minutes, fetching jobs due within roughly the next five minutes.
options_en: Poll the database every two seconds, fetching only jobs due within the next two seconds.
Poll every five minutes, fetching jobs due in roughly the next five minutes as a latency buffer.
Poll the database once an hour, fetching jobs due within the entire next hour.
Poll the database only once a day, fetching every job due that entire day.
optionExplanations: 每 2 秒查一次数据库，等于把第一层退化回原来那个压垮数据库的高频轮询。
对，每 5 分钟查一次、多留一点网络延迟缓冲，既减轻数据库压力又不会漏掉近期 Job。
取未来整整 1 小时的 Job，会让第二层队列堆积大量还早得很的消息，管理成本更高。
一天只查一次，绝大多数 Job 的调度时间会在被捞出来之前就已经过去了。
optionExplanations_en: Polling every 2 seconds just turns the first layer back into the same high-frequency query that was overwhelming the database.
Right: polling every 5 minutes with a bit of buffer for network delay cuts database load while still catching jobs due soon.
Pulling a full hour ahead would let the queue pile up with far-future messages that add management overhead for no benefit.
Polling only once a day means most jobs' scheduled times would already have passed before they're ever fetched.

scenario: 两层架构第一层是每 5 分钟一次的 cron，用户刚创建的 Job 却安排在 2 分钟后执行。
scenario_en: The first tier is a cron that runs every five minutes, but a user just created a job that is due in two minutes.
q: 新建的 Job 若安排在 5 分钟之内执行，为什么不能光靠「每 5 分钟的 cron」？
q_en: If a newly created job is due within five minutes, why can't the every-five-minutes cron alone handle it?
options: 是因为这个 cron 任务本身只负责处理周期性的 Job
cron 可能已经跑过、错过它，得等到下一轮（最多 5 分钟后）才被捞到
是因为数据库这时候会直接拒绝接受任何新的写入请求
是因为新创建的 Job 这时候其实还没有生成 job_id，所以根本没法被任何机制捞取
why: 若 cron 刚跑完，5 分钟内到期的新 Job 会被漏掉，最坏要等下一轮（5 分钟后）才捞到，违反 2 秒精度。所以要给近期 Job 特殊通道。
why_en: A job due within five minutes can be missed by the periodic cron and wait up to five minutes for the next run.
options_en: Because this cron job is itself only responsible for handling recurring jobs.
The cron may have already run and miss it, delaying up to five minutes to the next run.
Because the database would directly refuse to accept any new write requests at that point.
Because a newly created job does not actually have a job_id generated yet at that point., so no mechanism could pick it up at all.
optionExplanations: cron 一次性 Job 和周期性 Job 都会捞，这不是它漏检的原因。
对，cron 可能刚扫完就被创建，只能等下一轮，最坏要等满 5 分钟才被捞到。
写入这时候完全正常，数据库不会因为快到执行时间就拒绝新 Job 的创建请求。
Job 创建时就已经分配好 job_id，缺的不是 ID，是被捞取的时机。
optionExplanations_en: cron picks up one-time jobs too, not just periodic ones — that's not why it can miss things.
Right: if cron just finished its scan, a brand-new job has to wait for the next cycle — worst case, a full 5 minutes.
Writes work fine at that moment — the database doesn't reject new job creation just because execution time is near.
A job gets its job_id at creation time — what's missing isn't the ID, it's being picked up in time.

scenario: 用户新建一个安排在 3 分钟后执行的 Job，需要绕过「每 5 分钟 cron」的漏检窗口。
scenario_en: A user creates a job due to run in three minutes, which needs to bypass the blind spot of the every-five-minutes cron.
q: 应该怎么处理？
q_en: How should this be handled?
options: 把它直接写进 Kafka 某个分区的末尾，排队等前面的消息处理完
写库的同时，直接带上对应 delay 发到 SQS，绕过 cron
把 cron 的轮询频率直接改成每秒执行一次来兜底
直接拒绝创建这个调度时间太近的 Job 请求
why: 调度时间 < 5 分钟的新 Job，除了写库还要直接带 delay 推入 SQS，绕过 cron 的漏检窗口，保证及时执行。
why_en: A job scheduled within five minutes is written directly to SQS with the right delay, bypassing the periodic cron.
whenOtherWins: 调度时间在 5 分钟以外的 Job 则不必直投，交给 cron 定期扫描即可，避免队列里堆积过多远期消息。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    N["New job"] --> T{"Due within 5 min?"}
    T -->|yes| Q["Send to delay queue now"]
    T -->|no| DB[("Persist only")]
    DB --> C["Cron later enqueues"]
tradeoff: 近期 Job 直投队列 vs 远期 Job 交给周期 cron
options_en: Write it directly to the tail of a Kafka partition and let it wait behind everything already queued.
Persist it and also send it to SQS with the right delay, bypassing the cron.
Change the cron's polling frequency to run every single second as a fallback.
Simply refuse to create this job request because its scheduled time is too soon.
optionExplanations: Kafka 分区内严格按入队顺序执行，排在后面就只能等前面的处理完，帮不了近期 Job。
对，写库的同时直接带 delay 推 SQS，绕开 cron 的下一轮等待，近期 Job 立刻有了保底通道。
把 cron 改回秒级轮询，等于把第一层查库低频这个设计初衷整个推翻。
直接拒绝创建，把设计问题转嫁成了产品体验问题，不是真正的技术解法。
optionExplanations_en: Kafka executes strictly in enqueue order within a partition — sitting behind earlier messages doesn't help a near-term job.
Right: writing to the database and pushing to SQS with a matching delay at the same time skips cron's next-cycle wait entirely.
Switching cron back to per-second polling undoes the whole point of keeping the database poll infrequent.
Rejecting the job outright just turns a design problem into a bad user experience, not an actual fix.

scenario: 团队正在挑选支持「未来才执行」的延迟队列技术，有人提议直接复用现有的 Kafka 集群。
scenario_en: The team is choosing a delayed-delivery queue technology, and someone proposes just reusing the existing Kafka cluster.
q: 为什么不能简单地把「未来才执行的 Job」直接放进 Kafka 这类日志型队列？
q_en: Why can't jobs meant to run in the future simply be dropped into a log-based queue like Kafka?
options: Kafka 不支持持久化
Kafka 分区内严格有序，晚入队的排后面
Kafka 无法存 200 字节的小消息
Kafka 不支持多消费者
why: Kafka 分区内严格 FIFO，晚入队但该早执行的 Job 只能排在末尾等前面的跑完，无法按 execution_time 优先，破坏 2 秒精度。需要支持延迟投递的队列。
why_en: A log-based queue like Kafka delivers in order, so a job scheduled sooner still waits behind earlier-enqueued jobs.
options_en: Kafka does not support persistence.
Kafka delivers strictly in order per partition, so late arrivals queue behind it.
Kafka cannot store a 200-byte message.
Kafka does not support multiple consumers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分区内严格有序的分布式日志型消息队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed log-based queue that delivers messages in strict order within each partition.

optionExplanations: Kafka 本身就是靠持久化日志起家的，这不是它不适合本场景的原因。
对，Kafka 分区内严格按入队顺序投递，该早执行的 Job 只能排在后面等，做不到按执行时间抢先。
两百字节的小消息 Kafka 存起来毫无压力，大小从来不是问题。
Kafka 原生支持多个消费者组并行消费，这也不是它的短板。
optionExplanations_en: Kafka is built on a persistent log to begin with — that's not why it doesn't fit here.
Right: Kafka delivers strictly in enqueue order within a partition, so a job that should run sooner still waits behind whatever got queued first.
A 200-byte message is trivially small for Kafka to store — size was never the issue.
Kafka natively supports multiple consumer groups reading in parallel — that's not a shortcoming either.

scenario: 第一层已把未来 5 分钟的 Job 批量捞出，第二层要让每条只在自己那一秒才被消费。
scenario_en: The first tier has already pulled the next five minutes of jobs; the second tier must make each one consumable only at its own second.
q: 第二层队列需要的关键能力是什么？
q_en: What key capability does the second-layer queue need?
options: 消息在同一个分区内部必须严格按照入队的先后顺序做全局有序投递，这正是这一层恰恰不想要的行为
延迟投递（delayed delivery）：消息在接近执行时间时才对 Worker 可见
这一层队列需要原生支持复杂的关系型 SQL 查询和联表语法
这一层队列需要把系统里所有的消息都无限期地永久保留下来
why: 第二层需要延迟投递能力：让消息只在（接近）执行时间才对 Worker 可见，这样才能按 execution_time 精确触发，而非入队顺序。
why_en: The second layer needs delayed delivery so messages become visible to workers only near their scheduled time.
diagram:
flowchart TD
    D["Delay queue"] --> A["accept future timestamp"]
    D --> B["hide until due"]
    D --> C["deliver near due time"]
    D --> E["retry or DLQ on failure"]
options_en: Messages within the same partition must be delivered in strict, globally ordered enqueue sequence., which is exactly the behavior this layer wants to avoid.
Delayed delivery: messages become visible to workers only near their execution time.
This queue layer needs to natively support complex relational SQL queries and joins.
This queue layer needs to retain every message in the system forever, with no expiration at all.
optionExplanations: 严格按入队顺序投递恰恰是 Kafka 的问题所在，这层要的是反过来的能力。
对，消息得先「潜伏」着，快到点了才冒出来给 Worker 看见，靠的正是这份按时机现身的能力。
队列要做的是投递消息，不是承担关系型查询和 join 这种数据库的活。
消息被消费完该清理就清理，无限期保留只会让队列越堆越大。
optionExplanations_en: Strict enqueue-order delivery is exactly the problem with Kafka here — this layer needs the opposite capability.
Right: the message stays hidden until it's nearly due, then surfaces for a worker to grab — visibility keyed to timing, not queue position.
A queue's job is delivering messages, not taking on relational queries and joins — that's a database's job.
Messages should be cleaned up once consumed; keeping everything forever just lets the queue grow without bound.

scenario: 想在中等规模上用 Redis 实现延迟优先队列。
scenario_en: The team wants to implement a delayed priority queue with Redis at moderate scale.
q: 该用 Redis 的什么结构，代价是什么？
q_en: Which Redis structure should be used, and what's the cost?
options: 用 Redis List 做 FIFO，无需额外代码，但没办法按执行时间取出到期的项
Sorted Set（ZSET）按 execution_time 排序
用 Redis String 存所有 Job
用 Redis Pub/Sub 广播所有 Job
why: Redis ZSET 以执行时间戳为 score 做优先队列，Worker 取 score < 当前时间的项。性能极佳（亚毫秒、原子操作），但要自己写重试、故障处理、管理副本避免单点。
why_en: Redis sorted sets score jobs by execution time for a priority queue, but you must build retries, failure handling, and replication yourself.
whenOtherWins: 在允许托管服务、追求零运维的场景，SQS 原生延迟投递更省心；Redis 适合禁用托管服务或已有 Redis 专长的团队。
tradeoff: 自建 Redis 优先队列（高性能，高运维） vs 托管队列（省运维）
options_en: Use a Redis List as a FIFO, no extra code needed., but it can't pull out items whose time has come.
A sorted set (ZSET) ordered by execution_time.
Store every job as a Redis String.
Broadcast every job over Redis Pub/Sub.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的有序集合结构，按 score 排序存储成员。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ZSET is a Redis sorted set that orders its members by a numeric score.

optionExplanations: List 只能先进先出，没有『按执行时间取到期项』这种排序能力，帮不上忙。
对，ZSET 用执行时间戳当 score 做优先队列，取 score 小于当前时间的项，性能亚毫秒级。
一个 String 键存不下成千上万条独立的 Job，也没法按时间检索。
Pub/Sub 是广播、订阅者不在线就收不到，不是能按时间取货的持久化队列。
optionExplanations_en: A List is strictly FIFO with no notion of ordering by execution time — it doesn't help here.
Right: a ZSET uses the execution timestamp as the score to act as a priority queue, pulling entries with score below now — sub-millisecond performance.
A single String key can't hold thousands of independent jobs, nor be queried by time.
Pub/Sub is broadcast-only — a subscriber that's offline just misses the message; it's not a durable, time-addressable queue.

scenario: 考虑用 RabbitMQ 实现延迟投递。
scenario_en: The team is considering RabbitMQ for delayed message delivery.
q: RabbitMQ 实现延迟投递的典型方式及其难点是？
q_en: What's RabbitMQ's typical way of achieving delayed delivery, and what's the difficulty?
options: 以为有原生 delay 字段，零配置直接可用
TTL + 死信交换机（DLX）模拟延迟投递
照搬 Kafka 分区偏移量的思路来实现延迟
RabbitMQ 完全不支持任何形式的延迟投递
why: RabbitMQ 靠 TTL + 死信交换机模拟延迟投递；高可用需要额外配置 quorum queues，否则集群只复制拓扑不复制队列内容。
why_en: RabbitMQ can delay via per-message TTL plus a dead-letter exchange, but high availability requires quorum queues.
whenOtherWins: 如果团队已重度使用 RabbitMQ 并接受其运维复杂度，它也能胜任；否则 SQS 的原生延迟更简单。
tradeoff: 自建 RabbitMQ 延迟（可控但复杂） vs 托管队列原生延迟（简单省心）
options_en: Assuming there's a native delay field, ready to use with zero configuration.
Per-message TTL plus a dead-letter exchange (DLX) simulates delayed delivery.
Copying Kafka's partition-offset approach to implement delay.
RabbitMQ supports no form of delay whatsoever.

termDefinitions.meaning: 支持多种交换机路由模式的消息代理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RabbitMQ is a message broker that supports flexible exchange-based routing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消息或缓存条目的存活时间，到期后过期或被路由走。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the time-to-live after which a message or cache entry expires or gets rerouted.

termDefinitions.meaning: RabbitMQ 里接收过期或被拒消息、再转发到目标队列的交换机。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dead-letter exchange in RabbitMQ receives expired or rejected messages and reroutes them to a target queue.

termDefinitions.meaning: RabbitMQ 里基于多数派复制、保证队列内容高可用的队列类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Quorum queues are a RabbitMQ queue type that replicates content across a majority of nodes for high availability.

optionExplanations: 标准 RabbitMQ 并没有开箱即用的原生延迟字段，这个说法过于理想化。
对，靠给消息设 TTL、到期后转投死信交换机，间接模拟出延迟投递的效果。
Kafka 的分区偏移量是另一套系统的概念，照搬过来跟 RabbitMQ 的实现方式无关。
RabbitMQ 能做延迟，只是不是原生字段，得靠 TTL+DLX 这种组合技模拟。
optionExplanations_en: Stock RabbitMQ has no true zero-config native delay field — that's overselling it.
Right: setting a TTL and routing expired-timer messages through a dead-letter exchange simulates delayed delivery indirectly.
Kafka partition offsets belong to a different system entirely — copying that idea over has nothing to do with how RabbitMQ works.
RabbitMQ can do delay, just not as a native field — it takes the TTL-plus-DLX combination to simulate it.

scenario: 允许用托管服务、要求延迟投递 + 自动处理 Worker 失败 + 轻松扩到 10k/s，且尽量少运维。
scenario_en: Managed services are allowed, and the requirements are delayed delivery, automatic handling of worker failures, easy scaling to 10k/s, and minimal ops burden.
q: 作者最终为延迟队列选了哪个？
q_en: Which one does the author ultimately choose for the delay queue?
options: Amazon SQS（原生延迟投递 DelaySeconds + 可见性超时 + 死信队列）
自建的 Redis ZSET 优先队列，靠自己的代码管理重试和高可用
Kafka，一个分区内严格有序的分布式日志型消息队列
RabbitMQ 搭配死信交换机（DLX），并额外配置 quorum queues 保高可用
why: SQS 全托管、原生支持延迟投递（DelaySeconds）、用可见性超时自动处理 Worker 失败、死信队列兜底失败 Job、跨 AZ 高可用且自动扩展，最贴合需求。
why_en: Amazon SQS is chosen for native delayed delivery, visibility timeouts for worker failure, dead-letter queues, and automatic scaling.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官或公司禁止用托管服务（要开源自建），就改用 Redis 等自建优先队列——务必先问清楚限制。
tradeoff: 全托管队列（省运维） vs 自建队列（更可控但运维重）

rows: 跨 AZ 自动高可用

options_en: Amazon SQS: native delayed delivery, visibility timeouts, and dead-letter queues.
A self-built Redis ZSET priority queue, managing its own retries and high availability with custom code.
Kafka, a distributed log-based queue that delivers strictly in order within each partition.
RabbitMQ paired with a dead-letter exchange, plus quorum queues configured separately for high availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的全托管消息队列服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQS is Amazon's fully managed message queue service.

termDefinitions.meaning: SQS 消息的最小延迟投递参数，消息在这段时间内对消费者不可见。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DelaySeconds is an SQS parameter that keeps a message invisible to consumers for at least that many seconds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 超过重试上限的消息被转移进的兜底队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dead-letter queue catches messages that exceed the retry limit for later inspection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分区内严格有序的分布式日志型消息队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed log-based queue that delivers messages in strict order within each partition.

optionExplanations: 对，SQS 全托管，DelaySeconds 原生延迟、可见性超时兜底失败、死信队列收尾，几乎零运维就满足需求。
自建 Redis 优先队列性能极佳，但重试、故障转移、高可用都得自己写代码兜底，运维负担重。
Kafka 分区内严格有序，天然不适合『该早执行的 Job 要插到中间』这种延迟触发场景。
RabbitMQ 能靠 TTL+DLX 做延迟，但要扛高可用还得额外配 quorum queues，自建复杂度不低。
optionExplanations_en: Right: SQS is fully managed — native DelaySeconds, visibility timeout for failure handling, and a dead-letter queue on top — nearly zero ops for what's needed.
A self-built Redis priority queue performs great, but retries, failover, and high availability all become code you have to write and run yourself.
Kafka is strictly ordered within a partition, which is a bad fit for a job that needs to jump the queue and fire early.
RabbitMQ can simulate delay with TTL and a dead-letter exchange, but reaching high availability needs quorum queues on top — real operational weight.

scenario: 第一层 cron 只处理未来约 5 分钟内到期的 Job，随后把它们连同延迟时长送进 SQS。
scenario_en: The first-layer cron only handles jobs due within about the next five minutes, then sends them to SQS along with a delay value.
q: SQS 的 DelaySeconds（延迟投递）上限是多少，为什么这对本设计不成问题？
q_en: What's the cap on SQS's DelaySeconds, and why isn't it a problem for this design?
options: 上限只有 60 秒，覆盖不了我们的 5 分钟窗口，得拆成多次投递
上限 15 分钟，而我们只需在 5 分钟窗口内投递，绰绰有余
上限是 1 小时，刚好卡住我们需要的窗口边界，余量很紧
完全没有上限，可以设置任意长的延迟投递时间，更灵活
why: DelaySeconds 上限 15 分钟；我们的 cron 只处理未来 5 分钟内的 Job，所以 5 分钟窗口完全落在 15 分钟限制内。
why_en: SQS caps DelaySeconds at fifteen minutes, comfortably covering the five-minute scheduling window.
options_en: A 60-second cap, which cannot cover our five-minute window, so it'd have to be split into multiple deliveries.
A fifteen-minute cap, comfortably covering our five-minute window.
A one-hour cap, which just barely covers the window boundary we need, leaving little slack.
There is no cap at all; any arbitrarily long delay can be set, giving more flexibility.

termDefinitions.meaning: SQS 消息的最小延迟投递参数，消息在这段时间内对消费者不可见。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DelaySeconds is an SQS parameter that keeps a message invisible to consumers for at least that many seconds.

optionExplanations: 60 秒的上限远小于我们要投递的 5 分钟窗口，这个数字说反了，也不需要拆多次投递。
对，上限是 15 分钟，我们只需要覆盖 5 分钟窗口，还留了不少余量。
1 小时这个上限数字不对，会误导设计者以为窗口卡得很紧、其实还很宽松。
延迟投递不可能没有上限，SQS 明确写死了 15 分钟这个边界。
optionExplanations_en: 60 seconds is far smaller than the 5-minute window we need to cover — that number is wrong, and no splitting is actually needed.
Right: the cap is 15 minutes, and our window only needs 5, leaving plenty of headroom.
1 hour is the wrong number — it would mislead you into thinking the window is tightly bounded when it isn't.
Delayed delivery isn't unbounded — SQS hard-caps it at 15 minutes.

scenario: 第二层用 SQS 的 DelaySeconds 做延迟投递，而非功能指标是 2 秒执行精度。
scenario_en: The second tier uses SQS DelaySeconds for delayed delivery, against a two-second execution precision target.
q: 关于 SQS 的 DelaySeconds，下面哪句最准确？
q_en: Which statement about SQS's DelaySeconds is most accurate?
options: 它是一个能保证精确执行时刻的严格承诺
它是最小延迟而非精度保证，但因为 Worker 持续轮询，额外延迟通常可忽略
超过 DelaySeconds 之后消息会永久对所有消费者不可见
这个延迟投递参数只对 FIFO 队列类型生效，Standard 队列不支持
why: DelaySeconds 是「至少延迟这么久」的下限，不是精确触发保证；但由于 Worker 一直在轮询队列，超出的那点延迟通常可忽略不计。
why_en: DelaySeconds is a minimum delay rather than a precision guarantee, but continuous worker polling makes extra latency negligible.
options_en: It is a strict guarantee of the precise moment a message will be delivered.
It is a minimum delay, not a precision guarantee, but continuous polling makes the gap negligible.
Past DelaySeconds, the message becomes permanently invisible to every consumer.
This delay parameter only works on FIFO queues; Standard queues do not support it.

termDefinitions.meaning: SQS 消息的最小延迟投递参数，消息在这段时间内对消费者不可见。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DelaySeconds is an SQS parameter that keeps a message invisible to consumers for at least that many seconds.

optionExplanations: DelaySeconds 保证的是『至少等这么久』，不是精确到那一刻必然触发，说成严格承诺是夸大了。
对，它保证的是下限，不是精确那一刻；但队列本来就被不停巡查，多出来那点延迟基本感觉不到。
延迟期过后消息只是变得可见，之后一直等着被消费，不会永久对谁都不可见。
Standard 和 FIFO 队列都支持 DelaySeconds，不是 FIFO 独有的能力。
optionExplanations_en: DelaySeconds guarantees 'at least this long,' not a precise trigger at that exact moment — calling it a strict promise overstates it.
Right: it's a floor on delay, not a precision guarantee, but since workers keep polling continuously, the extra lag is basically negligible.
Once the delay passes, the message just becomes visible and waits to be consumed — it doesn't go permanently invisible to everyone.
Both Standard and FIFO queues support DelaySeconds — it isn't FIFO-exclusive.

scenario: 架构图画完，面试官说「现在把它扩到 10k Job/s」，要你系统性地找出瓶颈在哪。
scenario_en: With the architecture drawn, the interviewer says scale this to 10k jobs per second and wants you to locate the bottlenecks systematically.
q: 在扩展性深潜里，作者建议排查瓶颈的方法是？
q_en: In the scalability deep dive, what method does the author recommend for hunting down bottlenecks?
options: 先优化数据库，其他不管
从左到右沿数据流逐个组件排查瓶颈，逐一解决
一次性把所有组件都加缓存
只关注 Worker 层，完全不管前面数据库和队列可能先出问题
why: 谈扩展时从左到右沿数据流走一遍，逐个组件找瓶颈并解决：Job 创建 → 数据库 → 消息队列 → Worker。
why_en: For scaling, walk left to right along the data flow and address each component's bottleneck one by one.
options_en: Only optimize the database and ignore the rest.
Walk left to right along the data flow, addressing each component's bottleneck.
Add caching to every component at once.
Only focus on the worker layer., ignoring that the database or queue upstream might buckle first.
optionExplanations: 只盯着数据库优化，会漏掉队列、Worker 这些同样可能先撑不住的环节。
对，沿数据流从创建到数据库、队列、Worker 依次走一遍，逐个组件揪出真正的瓶颈再解决。
一次性给所有组件都加缓存，既没先定位真实瓶颈，也可能为不需要的地方增加复杂度。
只看 Worker 层会忽略前面数据库和队列可能才是先撑不住的地方。
optionExplanations_en: Fixating on the database alone misses the queue or the worker layer, which might buckle first instead.
Right: walk the data flow in order — creation, database, queue, worker — and find and fix the real bottleneck at each stage.
Caching everything at once skips actually locating the real bottleneck, and adds complexity where it may not be needed.
Looking only at workers ignores that the database or queue upstream might be the one hitting its limit first.

scenario: 系统的执行吞吐上限是 10k Job/秒，其中相当一部分执行来自周期性 Job 的重复实例，而非新建请求。
scenario_en: The system's execution throughput cap is 10k jobs per second, and a good share of those executions come from recurring jobs' repeat instances rather than brand-new requests.
q: 为什么说「10k Job 创建/秒」只是 Job 创建量的上界、通常达不到？
q_en: Why is '10k job creations per second' only an upper bound on creation volume that's usually not actually reached?
options: 是因为数据库本身的写入能力根本达不到这个速度
因为支持周期性 Job，很多执行来自重复实例而非新建，实际新建量往往更低
是因为这套系统的注册用户数量本身就非常少
是因为 API 网关这一层对创建请求做了严格限流，把大部分请求都拦在了外面
why: 10k/s 是执行量。由于支持周期性 Job，很多执行来自复用的定义而非新建，所以创建量通常低于 10k/s——除非绝大多数是一次性 Job，那时创建服务才可能成瓶颈。
why_en: Because recurring jobs reuse definitions, actual job creation is usually below the 10k-per-second execution upper bound.
options_en: Because the database's own write capacity simply cannot reach that speed.
Because recurring jobs reuse definitions, so actual creation volume is usually lower than the 10k/s execution bound.
Because the number of registered users on this system is simply very small.
Because the API gateway layer applies strict rate limiting to creation requests., blocking most requests before they even land.
optionExplanations: 10k/s 说的是执行吞吐，不是在断言数据库写入能力达不到，这个理由文不对题。
对，很多执行来自周期性 Job 反复复用同一份定义，真正的『新建』请求量通常比执行量低得多。
创建量和执行量的差距，跟注册用户多少没有直接关系，关键在 Job 是否周期性复用。
题目没有说网关在限流，这只是凭空加了一个不存在的约束。
optionExplanations_en: 10k/s describes execution throughput, not a claim about database write capacity — that reasoning is off-target.
Right: a lot of execution comes from periodic jobs reusing the same definition, so actual 'create' traffic usually runs well below execution volume.
The gap between creation and execution volume isn't about how many users are registered — it's about whether jobs recur.
Nothing in the scenario says the gateway is rate-limiting — that's inventing a constraint that isn't there.

scenario: 在扩展 Job 创建时，有人提议在 API 与 Job 创建服务之间加一层 Kafka 做缓冲。
scenario_en: While scaling job creation, someone proposes adding a Kafka buffering layer between the API and the job creation service.
q: 作者对此的立场是？
q_en: What's the author's stance on this?
options: 必须无条件加上这层队列，否则系统在高负载下一定会崩溃，没有任何例外情况可言，即便业务逻辑很轻也不能省
多半是过度设计：数据库能直接扛写入、服务本可水平扩展，除非有昂贵业务逻辑要隔离，否则保持简单
应该在 API 和数据库之间再叠加两层不同的消息队列
消息队列这时候完全可以替代数据库承担持久化的职责
why: 加 Kafka 缓冲通常是过度设计：数据库能直接承接写入，前面的服务本就可水平扩展。除非创建服务里有昂贵业务逻辑要隔离，否则先把数据库和服务层扩好，保持架构简单。
why_en: Buffering job creation with a queue is usually overcomplication since the database and a horizontally scaled service suffice.
whenOtherWins: 如果创建路径里有昂贵、易失败的业务逻辑需要削峰和隔离，或写入确实突发到压垮数据库，加缓冲队列才划算。
tradeoff: 简单直接（服务+数据库） vs 额外缓冲队列（隔离但更复杂）
options_en: This queue layer must be added unconditionally, or the system will definitely crash under load., with no exceptions allowed at all., even when the business logic itself is trivially light.
Usually overcomplication: the database and a horizontally scaled service already suffice.
Two separate layers of message queues should be stacked between the API and the database.
A message queue could fully replace the database's job of persisting data at this point.
optionExplanations: 把它说成『不加就必崩』过于绝对，实际上数据库和服务层本身就有扩展空间。
对，多数情况是过度设计：数据库能直接扛写入，服务可水平扩展；除非有昂贵逻辑要隔离，否则没必要多绕一层。
在 API 和数据库之间叠两层不同队列，只会让链路更长、故障排查更难，没有对应的收益。
队列擅长缓冲和传递消息，但不提供数据库那种可查询、可持久化的存储能力，替代不了它。
optionExplanations_en: Calling it 'must-add or it crashes' is too absolute — the database and service layer already have room to scale on their own.
Right: it's usually over-engineering — the database can take writes directly and the service scales horizontally, so skip the extra hop unless there's expensive logic to isolate.
Stacking two different queues between the API and the database just lengthens the path and complicates debugging, with no matching payoff.
A queue is good at buffering and passing messages, but it doesn't give you a database's queryable, durable storage — it can't replace that role.

scenario: Jobs 表按 job_id 分区，Executions 表按 time_bucket 分区；DynamoDB 单个分区的写容量存在上限（约 1,000 WCU）。
scenario_en: The Jobs table partitions by job_id and Executions by time_bucket; a single DynamoDB partition has a write-capacity cap of roughly 1,000 WCU.
q: 这个分区级写容量上限，对分区键设计提出了什么要求？
q_en: What does this per-partition write-capacity cap demand from the partition key design?
options: 分区键必须让写入天然分散到多个分区，否则会撞上限
只要提高读容量就能绕开这个限制
换成 SSD 存储就没有这个限制
分区键随便选，DynamoDB 会自动无限扩容单分区
why: 单分区写容量有限，所以分区键要能让写入自然打散——job_id 唯一天然分散，time_bucket 则可能集中，需要写分片来补。
why_en: Because a single partition's write capacity is capped, the partition key must spread writes naturally across many partitions.
options_en: The partition key must let writes spread naturally, or it will hit the limit.
Just raising read capacity works around it.
Switching to SSD storage removes the limit.
The partition key does not matter; DynamoDB auto-scales a single partition without limit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写容量单位，衡量 DynamoDB 一个分区每秒能承受的写入量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WCU, or write capacity unit, measures how much write throughput a DynamoDB partition can absorb per second.

optionExplanations: 对，单分区写容量有限，分区键选不好、写入扎堆，很快就会撞上这条约 1000 WCU 的天花板。
读容量和写容量是两条独立的配额，提高读容量完全绕不开单分区写入上限。
分区写容量上限是 DynamoDB 的架构约束，不是底层用 HDD 还是 SSD 决定的。
单个分区并不会无限扩容，选错分区键、写入不均匀照样会被限流。
optionExplanations_en: Right: a single partition's write capacity is capped, so a poorly chosen key that clusters writes will quickly hit that roughly 1,000 WCU ceiling.
Read and write capacity are separate quotas — raising read capacity does nothing about a single partition's write cap.
That per-partition write ceiling is a DynamoDB architectural constraint, not something storage media like SSD changes.
A single partition doesn't scale without bound — pick a bad key with uneven writes and you'll still get throttled.

scenario: Executions 表按 time_bucket 分区，当前小时的所有写入都砸向同一个分区，形成热分区。
scenario_en: The Executions table partitions by time_bucket, so every write in the current hour lands on the same partition, forming a hot partition.
q: 怎么缓解这个热分区？
q_en: How do you relieve this hot partition?
options: 改用 job_id 作 Executions 分区键
写分片：分区键加随机后缀，写入分散到多分区
把整表搬到内存
降低写入速率
why: 写分片：在 time_bucket 后加随机后缀（time_bucket#shard_3）把同一小时的写分散到多个分区；读取时 Worker 并行查该时间桶的所有分片再合并。
why_en: Write sharding appends a random suffix to the time_bucket so writes spread across partitions, with workers querying all shards in parallel.
whenOtherWins: 如果写入量本就均匀、单分区没到 1,000 WCU，就无需分片——分片会增加读放大（要查多个分片）。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    B["time_bucket"] --> H["hot partition"]
    H --> S1["bucket#0"]
    H --> S2["bucket#1"]
    H --> S3["bucket#N"]
    S1 --> P1[("partition")]
    S2 --> P2[("partition")]
    S3 --> P3[("partition")]
tradeoff: 写分片分散热点 vs 读取要并行查多个分片
options_en: Switch the Executions table to job_id as partition key.
Write sharding: append a random suffix to the partition key so writes spread out.
Move the entire table into memory.
Reduce the write rate.
optionExplanations: 换成 job_id 会让『按时间桶找即将执行的 Job』这条主查询路径直接失效，代价太大。
对，给分区键加随机后缀把写入摊到多个分区，读时并行查这些分片再合并结果。
把整张表搬进内存既没有持久化，也不是 DynamoDB 分区容量问题的解法。
刻意压低写入速率是在回避业务需求，不是解决分区容量这个架构问题。
optionExplanations_en: Switching to job_id would break the primary 'find what's due by time bucket' query outright — too big a cost.
Right: adding a random suffix to the partition key spreads writes across multiple partitions, and reads fan out across those shards and merge the results.
Moving the whole table into memory has no durability and doesn't actually address DynamoDB's partition capacity limit.
Deliberately throttling write rate dodges the business requirement instead of solving the underlying capacity problem.

scenario: 为解热分区，time_bucket 加了随机后缀拆成 N 个分片，Worker 仍要取齐该桶全部到期 Job。
scenario_en: To break the hot partition, time_bucket got a random suffix splitting it into N shards, yet workers still need every due job in that bucket.
q: 给 Executions 表做写分片后，Worker 读取时要相应做什么？
q_en: After write-sharding the Executions table, what must workers do differently when reading?
options: 只查一个分片即可，其余分片的记录可以忽略
并行查询某个时间桶下的所有分片，再合并结果
改成全表扫描，放弃 time_bucket 分区带来的效率
写分片后不再需要查 Executions 表，改读缓存即可
why: 写分片把一个时间桶拆成多个分区，所以 Worker 要并行查该桶所有分片再合并，这是分片带来的读放大代价。
why_en: After write sharding, workers must query all shards of a time bucket in parallel and merge the results.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    W["Worker window"] --> R0["read shard 0"]
    W --> R1["read shard 1"]
    W --> RN["read shard N"]
    R0 --> M["merge due executions"]
    R1 --> M
    RN --> M
    M --> Q["enqueue"]
options_en: Query only a single shard, treating records in the other shards as ignorable.
Query all shards of a time bucket in parallel and merge the results.
Fall back to a full table scan, giving up the efficiency time_bucket partitioning bought.
After write sharding, the Executions table no longer needs querying — read from a cache instead.
optionExplanations: 只查一个分片会漏掉分散在其他分片里的执行记录，结果不完整。
对，Worker 要并行查该时间桶下的所有分片再合并，这是分片换来分散写入的读放大代价。
改成全表扫描完全丢掉了按 time_bucket 分区带来的效率优势，得不偿失。
写分片只是改变了数据的物理分布，Executions 表该查还是要查，没有缓存能替代它。
optionExplanations_en: Querying just one shard misses execution records scattered across the others — the result is incomplete.
Right: the worker fans out across every shard in that time bucket in parallel and merges the results — that's the read amplification cost sharding trades for spread-out writes.
Switching to a full table scan throws away all the efficiency that time_bucket partitioning was buying — not worth the tradeoff.
Write sharding only changes physical data placement — the Executions table still has to be queried, and no cache substitutes for it.

scenario: 已执行完的 Job 要保留供用户查询，但长期堆在主表里成本高。
scenario_en: Completed jobs must stay queryable for users, but leaving them in the main table long-term is costly.
q: 合理的数据生命周期策略是？
q_en: What's a sensible data lifecycle policy?
options: Job 一旦执行完毕就立刻把它的记录从数据库里删除
近期保留在主表；过了合理期限（如 1 年）迁到更便宜的存储如 S3
不论新旧，把所有 Job 记录永久留在 DynamoDB 主表里
只保留执行失败的 Job 记录，成功的 Job 记录直接丢弃
why: 执行完的 Job 短期留主表供查询，超过合理期限（如 1 年）后迁到 S3 这类廉价存储，兼顾可查询性与成本。
why_en: Keep recent executed jobs queryable, then archive older ones (after about a year) to cheaper storage like S3.
whenOtherWins: 若合规要求随时快速查询历史全量，或数据量小到成本可忽略，就没必要下沉冷存储。
tradeoff: 可查询性（主表） vs 存储成本（冷归档）
options_en: Delete a job's record from the database the instant it finishes executing.
Keep recent jobs queryable in the main table; archive older ones (say, after a year) to cheaper storage like S3.
Keep every job record, old or new, permanently in the DynamoDB main table forever.
Only keep records for jobs that failed, and discard the records of successful ones.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的对象存储服务，常用于低成本长期存档。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: S3 is AWS's object storage service, commonly used for low-cost long-term archiving.

optionExplanations: 跑完就删会让用户连自己刚执行完的 Job 记录都查不到，牺牲了可查询性。
对，近期记录留在主表方便查询，过了合理期限（如 1 年）迁到 S3 这类便宜存储，兼顾成本和可用性。
所有记录永久留在 DynamoDB 主表，存储成本会随时间线性甚至更快地膨胀。
只留失败记录会让用户没法确认成功的 Job 到底跑没跑、跑了几次，丢了审计能力。
optionExplanations_en: Deleting right after completion means a user can't even look up a job they just ran — that gives up queryability entirely.
Right: keep recent records in the main table for easy lookup, then archive to cheap storage like S3 past a retention window (say, a year) — balancing cost against usability.
Keeping every record forever in the main DynamoDB table lets storage cost grow linearly or worse over time.
Keeping only failures means users can't confirm whether a successful job actually ran or how many times — that loses the audit trail.

scenario: 10k Job/秒执行，5 分钟窗口内约产生 300 万条消息，每条约 200 字节（只含 job_id、执行时间和少量元数据）。
